name: Text complexity
note: Draft rubric. Levels and criteria follow the Learning Commons text complexity evaluators; the wording is ours.

sentence_structure.question: How hard are the sentences to follow?

levels.slightly_complex: Mostly short, simple sentences with one idea each and few or no subordinate clauses.
levels.moderately_complex: A mix of simple and compound sentences; some sentences have one subordinate clause.
levels.very_complex: Many complex sentences, often with two or more clauses or a long phrase before the main verb.
levels.exceedingly_complex: Most sentences are long and layered, with several embedded clauses the reader must hold in mind.

levels.slightly_complex: Everyday words a young reader already knows; almost no academic or subject-specific terms.
levels.moderately_complex: Some words that may be unfamiliar or academic, but context explains most of them.
levels.very_complex: Fairly many words that may be unfamiliar or academic, and context helps with some of them.
levels.exceedingly_complex: Dense with rare, technical, or abstract words, mostly unexplained, that many readers will not know.

background_knowledge.question: How much does the reader need to know already?

levels.slightly_complex: Everyday experiences; no outside knowledge needed.
levels.moderately_complex: Some common school knowledge, explained or easy to infer.
levels.very_complex: Subject knowledge the text assumes and does not explain.
levels.exceedingly_complex: Specialized or discipline-specific knowledge, with references the text never unpacks.
